interface.title: Cygnet — A Network of Signs (OMW Cygnet wordnet browser)
interface.stage_of_work: Looking things up and exploring a reference resource (lexicon lookup and checking where the data came from)
interface.what_it_is_for: A browser for a merged multilingual wordnet. You search for senses by exact word, wildcard pattern, Interlingual Index (ILI) id or definition text, filter by language or part of speech, and open a concept to see its definitions, relations, the words that express it in each language, and which source wordnet each record came from.

data.note: This is the seeded test database, not the real ~180,000-concept Cygnet database. It holds 3 wordnets: a CILI record, a Test English WordNet (9 concepts / 9 senses) and a Test French WordNet (1 concept, 'chien'). Concepts: entity, animal, dog (variant 'doggo'), dogfish, brightness, mouse, bright, gleaming and glowing. Pronunciation data is empty, so the 'Show pronunciation' setting made no visible difference. The About page reports 3 wordnets, 2 languages, 9 concepts, 10 entries and 10 senses (screens/047.webp).

tree.general: Find how a meaning is expressed in words across languages, and where each piece of lexical data came from
tree.specific: Search the merged Cygnet wordnet, inspect concepts, their relations and translations, and trace records back to their source wordnets

features.name: Single search box with query syntax detected automatically
features.general: One text box that works out from what you type whether you want an exact term, a pattern, an identifier lookup or a full-text search of descriptions, and puts the results in a link you can share
features.specific: Search box that accepts 'dog' (exact lemma), 'dog*' / '*ness' / 'chie?' (wildcards), 'i3' / 'cili.i3' (ILI lookup) or 'def:animal' (gloss search), with the state kept in the #/search?q= URL; a query with no match shows 'No results found for …'
steps: Type a query in the chosen syntax
Press Enter
Read the result count and the grouped senses
Change the syntax to switch mode (e.g. add * or def:)
serves_tasks: Look up an exact word and see its meanings and definitions
Find related word forms with a pattern
Look up a concept directly by its cross-language identifier
Find concepts whose definitions mention a term

features.name: Search facet filters with per-facet clear
features.general: Checkbox facets that narrow results by language or by grammatical category, updating the results at once and recording the filter in the shareable link. A dot on the settings icon shows when filters are on, and each facet has its own clear link
features.specific: ⚙ Settings: Language and Part-of-speech checkboxes, each with a 'clear' link; ticking one adds search_lang= or pos= to the URL and lights a dot on ⚙
steps: Open ⚙ Settings
Tick a language or part-of-speech facet; results update at once and the URL gets search_lang= or pos=
Check the dot on ⚙ that marks active filters
Press 'clear' next to a facet to drop it
serves_tasks: Restrict results to one part of speech

features.name: Display language with marked fallback
features.general: Choose the language used for labels and descriptions; where a translation is missing the original-language text is shown instead and visibly tagged, with a note explaining the fallback
features.specific: ⚙ Settings 'Display results in' dropdown: senses are relabelled (dog → chien), untranslated labels and definitions carry an [en] tag, and the URL gains display_lang=
steps: Open ⚙ Settings
Choose a language in 'Display results in'
Read the relabelled senses and definitions, noting the [en] tags on English fallbacks
serves_tasks: Show labels and definitions in another language

features.name: Per-record source tags
features.general: A toggle that labels each description, link and word form with the dataset that contributed it, so every record in a merged resource can be traced to its origin
features.specific: ⚙ Settings 'Show sources': definitions, relations and forms in the concept view carry (wn-en:1.0) / (wn-fr:1.0) tags
steps: Open ⚙ Settings and tick 'Show sources'
Open a concept
Read the source tag after each definition, relation and form
serves_tasks: Trace each record back to the source dataset that contributed it

features.name: Grouped, collapsible result list with expandable rows
features.general: Results are grouped in two levels (by language, then by category). Each group can be collapsed, and each row can be expanded to show extra links that run a new search or open a detail view
features.specific: Language cards (English/French) containing part-of-speech sub-groups (Noun/Adjective). Each sense row has a ▶ toggle that shows 'Variants' or sense relations such as 'opposite'. Clicking a relation opens a 'Filtered to a single sense' view with 'Clear filter'
steps: Run a search
Collapse or expand a language card or part-of-speech group with ▼/▶
Expand a sense row with ▶ to see variants or sense relations
Click a variant or related sense to jump to it, or click the sense card to open its concept
serves_tasks: Collapse groups of results to focus on one part
Look up an exact word and see its meanings and definitions
Open a concept and compare how each language expresses it

features.name: Concept view with relation display modes and forms in each language
features.general: A detail page for one concept with a three-way toggle for how linked items are shown (graph, text list or hidden), clickable links to move to neighbouring concepts, and a list of the words that express the concept in each language
features.specific: Concept view: definition with ⟪ILI⟫ badge, Related Concepts toggle (Graph / Text / None; default set by ⚙ Settings 'Related concepts') listing class hypernym, class hyponym, equivalent synonym and 'related through senses' links, and 'All forms expressing this concept' grouped by language
steps: Click a sense in the results to open its concept view
Switch Related Concepts between Graph, Text and None
Click a related concept to move up or down the hierarchy
Click a form in another language to open search results filtered to that sense
Press '← Back to search' to return to the results
serves_tasks: Open a concept and compare how each language expresses it
Inspect broader and narrower concepts and move along the hierarchy
Explore linked concepts as an interactive network diagram

features.name: Path finder between two concepts
features.general: Pick a second item with an autocomplete box (by name or identifier) and get the shortest chain of typed links from the current item to it, shown as clickable chips. It reports when no path exists within a step limit
features.specific: 'Path to concept': type a word or ILI, pick from the suggestions (each shows its part of speech and gloss), press Find path, and read a chip chain such as dog —class hypernym→ animal —class hypernym→ entity, or 'No path found within 12 steps'
steps: Type a word or ILI id in the path box
Click the matching suggestion (an ILI id resolves to its concept directly)
Press Find path
Read the chain of relation-labelled chips, or the no-path message
Click a chip to open that concept
serves_tasks: Find the chain of relations linking two concepts
Inspect broader and narrower concepts and move along the hierarchy

features.name: Source-dataset inventory with per-source summary pages
features.general: A table of the datasets merged into the resource, with counts, version, citation and licence. A hover tooltip gives a quick summary and a click opens a full coverage report (counts, breakdown by category, relation-type counts with example links into the data)
features.specific: Wordnets tab: Contributing Wordnets table, ⓘ hover tooltip, and a summary page per wordnet (Metadata, Coverage tiles for Concepts / Senses / ILI % / Definitions / Examples, Part of speech table, Semantic and Sense relations tables with example links)
steps: Open the Wordnets tab
Hover ⓘ on a row for a quick summary
Click ⓘ for the full summary page
Click an example lemma or relation example to open that concept
serves_tasks: See which datasets contributed and how much each covers
Trace each record back to the source dataset that contributed it

The graph library probably did not load in this offline setting. Kept in the tree as stub task n1.
Database downloads (cygnet.db.gz, provenance.db.gz) on the About page: the links point off-site, the browser landed on an error page (screens/048.webp) and nothing was downloaded.
Pronunciation display: the test data has no pronunciations, so the 'Show pronunciation' setting changed nothing visible.
not_done: Could not explore the graph-view relation explorer (hover to expand nodes) because the graph never drew.
Could not compare a concept across 40+ languages: the test database has only English and French, and only one French sense (chien).

The language filter applies to the language of the matched text. 'def:animal' with French ticked gave no results because the French wordnet has no definitions (screens/027.webp), so gloss search cannot be combined with a French-only filter on this data.

Clicking a form link in the concept view (e.g. French chien₁) dropped the active language filter (search_lang left the URL and the French checkbox was unticked afterwards). I noted this but did not investigate further.
The Path-to-concept autocomplete does not respond to the keyboard (ArrowDown + Enter did nothing); a suggestion has to be clicked.
The main search box has no autocomplete; I typed 'do' and no suggestions appeared.
Did not open the CILI and 'mtg' rows' summary pages or the external citation and licence links, which lead off-site.

Did not reach the separate sense view (#/search?sense=, a single word-sense with its synonyms, examples, pronunciations and sense relations). Clicking a form or related sense opened a 'Filtered to a single sense' result list instead (screens/033.webp); whether clicking the subscript sense label opens the sense view was not checked.
